items.title: Section: Fascicle Forty-One Opens — The Structure of the Forty-Three Minor Precepts

items.zh: 如是菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於有違犯及無違犯，是染非染、軟中上品，應當了知。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts should clearly understand, regarding any given matter, whether it constitutes a violation or not, whether it is tainted or untainted by affliction, and whether it falls into a mild, moderate, or severe degree.

items.title: Section: Precept One — Never a Day Without Genuine Reverence for the Three Jewels

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，於日日中，若於如來、或為如來造制多所；若於正法、或為正法造經卷所，謂諸菩薩素怛纜藏、摩怛理迦；若於僧伽，謂十方界已入大地諸菩薩眾。若不以其或少、或多諸供養具而為供養，下至以身一拜禮敬，下至以語一四句頌讚佛法僧真實功德，下至以心一清淨信隨念三寶真實功德，空度日夜，是名有犯，有所違越。
items.en: Bodhisattvas abiding in the bodhisattva precepts, every single day, towards the Tathāgata or a monument built for the Tathāgata, towards the true teaching or a scripture recording it, and towards the noble community — the bodhisattvas already established on the noble grounds across the ten directions — should make some offering, whether modest or abundant; at the very least, a single bow of respect, a single four-line verse praising the genuine qualities of the Buddha, the teaching, and the community, or, at the least, a single moment of pure faith calling those genuine qualities to mind. Letting an entire day and night pass with none of this at all constitutes a violation.

items.zh: 若不恭敬、嬾惰懈怠而違犯者，是染違犯。若誤失念而違犯者，非染違犯。

items.title: Section: When There Is No Violation — Genuine Illness, and an Advanced Bodhisattva's Natural, Unbroken Reverence

items.en: There is no violation for one whose mind is genuinely deranged.

items.zh: 若已證入淨意樂地，常無違犯。由得清淨意樂菩薩，譬如已得證淨苾芻，恒時法爾於佛法僧以勝供具承事供養。
items.en: Should a bodhisattva have already entered the ground of purified aspiration, there is never any violation at all — a bodhisattva of such purified aspiration, exactly as a monastic who has attained the four confirmed faiths — a stream-enterer — naturally and spontaneously serves and reveres the Buddha, the teaching, and the community with the finest offerings at every moment.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，有其大欲而無喜足，於諸利養及以恭敬生著不捨。是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。

items.title: Section: Precept Two Closes — Struggling Against Deep-Rooted Craving Is Not Yet a Fault

items.zh: 無違犯者，謂為斷彼，生起樂欲，發勤精進攝彼對治。雖勤遮遏，而為猛利性惑所蔽，數起現行。
items.en: There is no violation for one who, wishing to overcome this craving, diligently applies themselves to its antidote — even if, despite this sincere effort, the intense, innate affliction still repeatedly breaks through and manifests.

items.title: Section: Precept Three — Welcoming Elders and Fellow Practitioners With Genuine Courtesy

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，見諸耆長有德可敬同法者來，憍慢所制，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，不起承迎，不推勝座。若有他來語言談論、慶慰、請問，憍慢所制，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，不稱正理發言酬對。是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, seeing a respected elder or genuinely admirable fellow practitioner arrive, who, overcome by arrogance and harbouring resentment or irritation, do not rise to greet them or offer them the better seat ... this constitutes a tainted violation.

items.zh: 非憍慢制，無嫌恨心、無恚惱心，但由嬾惰、懈怠、忘念、無記之心，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。無違犯者，謂遭重病；或心狂亂；或自睡眠他生覺想，而來親附語言談論、慶慰、請問；或自為他宣說諸法論義決擇；或復與餘談論、慶慰；或他說法論義決擇屬耳而聽；或有違犯說正法者，為欲將護說法者心；或欲方便調彼、伏彼，出不善處安立善處；或護僧制；或為將護多有情心；而不酬對，皆無違犯。
items.en: Should this arise not from arrogance or resentment, but simply from laziness, forgetfulness, or genuine unfamiliarity with what to do, this is an untainted violation.

items.title: Section: Precept Four — Accepting Genuine Invitations

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，他來延請，或往居家、或往餘寺，奉施飲食及衣服等諸資生具，憍慢所制，懷嫌恨心、懷恚惱心，不至其所，不受所請，是名有犯，有所違越，是染違犯。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, invited to a home or another temple to receive food, clothing, or other necessities, who, overcome by arrogance and harbouring resentment, refuse to go or accept the invitation — this constitutes a tainted violation.

items.zh: 若由嬾惰、懈怠、忘念、無記之心，不至其所，不受所請，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。
無違犯者，或有疾病；或無氣力，或心狂亂；或處懸遠；或道有怖；或欲方便調彼、伏彼，出不善處安立善處；或餘先請；或為無間修諸善法，欲護善品令無暫廢；或為引攝未曾有義；或為所聞法義無退；如為所聞法義無退，論義決擇，當知亦爾；或復知彼懷損惱心，詐來延請；或為護他多嫌恨心；或護僧制；不至其所，不受所請，皆無違犯。
items.en: There is no violation for one who is ill, without strength, mentally deranged, invited somewhere too distant, facing genuine danger on the road, declining in order to skilfully correct the host instead, already committed elsewhere, protecting an unbroken course of meditative practice ... aware the invitation is offered in bad faith, protecting others from resentment, or observing the community's own formal discipline.

items.title: Section: Precept Five — Accepting Valuable Gifts, Where Refusal Out of Resentment "Abandons the Being"

items.zh: 若諸菩薩安住菩薩淨戒律儀，他持種種生色可染、末尼、真珠、琉璃等寶，及持種種眾多上妙財利供具慇懃奉施，由嫌恨心、或恚惱心，違拒不受，是名有犯，有所違越。是染違犯，捨有情故。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, offered gold and silver, maṇi jewels, pearls, beryl, and other treasures, or abundant, excellent material support with genuine sincerity, who refuse it out of resentment or irritation — this constitutes a tainted violation, since it amounts to abandoning the very being making the offering.

items.zh: 若由嬾惰、懈怠、忘念、無記之心，違拒不受，是名有犯，有所違越，非染違犯。
無違犯者，或心狂亂；或觀受已心生染著；或觀後時彼定追悔；或復知彼於施迷亂；或知施主隨捨隨受，由是因緣定當貧匱；或知此物是僧伽物、窣堵波物；或知此物劫盜他得；或知此物由是因緣多生過患，或殺、或縛、或罰、或黜、或嫌、或責；違拒不受，皆無違犯。
items.en: There is no violation for one who is mentally deranged, who foresees genuine attachment would arise from accepting it, who foresees the giver would surely come to regret it, who recognises the giver is giving by mistake, in a moment of confusion, who knows accepting would leave the giver genuinely impoverished, who recognises the object belongs to the community or a monument, who knows it was obtained through theft, or who foresees accepting it would lead to real harm — being killed, bound, punished, removed from office, resented, or blamed.

blocks.text: Fascicle 41 sets out the **lighter offences** of the bodhisattva precepts (often counted as forty-three; Master Cháng Bǎi: the commonly recited version has forty-one, and the commentaries count forty-two or forty-three). For each, the treatise says when it is an offence, whether it is "tainted" by affliction or not, and when there is no offence at all. That last part makes these precepts unusually humane.

One should know "whether it is a violation or not, tainted or untainted, mild, middling, or severe". Master Cháng Bǎi: breaking a precept from afflicted contempt is tainted; from ignorance or negligence, untainted.

Every day, towards the Buddha or a stupa, the Dharma or a scripture, the Saṅgha, one makes some offering, "even one prostration or one verse of praise". Failing this from disrespect is tainted; from forgetfulness, untainted. No offence for one "whose mind is genuinely deranged", nor for a bodhisattva of purified intention, whose reverence never lapses (Master Cháng Bǎi: like a stream-enterer, who has "unbreakable faith").

Great desire and discontent are offences; but "there is no violation for one who, wishing to overcome this craving, diligently applies its antidote", even if the innate affliction still arises. Master Cháng Bǎi: innate affliction is the momentum of past lives.
Not rising to greet an elder or fellow practitioner "out of arrogance or resentment" is tainted; "simply from laziness or forgetfulness", untainted. Venerable Miào Jìng comments on age.

Refusing an invitation out of pride is an offence; but not if ill, the distance is too great, the road dangerous, or one is in a retreat (Master Cháng Bǎi). Refusing a sincere gift of treasure out of resentment "amounts to abandoning the being"; not an offence if accepting would bring attachment or the giver would regret it.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, how many minor bodhisattva precepts are counted in different sources?
options: forty-one in the usual recitation text, forty-three in the 《瑜伽論記》, forty-two in the 《披尋記》
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the commonly recited bodhisattva precepts have only forty-one minor precepts; the 《瑜伽論記》 groups them as forty-three, the 《披尋記》 as forty-two.

quiz.q: "Tainted or untainted" — how do the lectures distinguish them?
options: violation with afflicted contempt is tainted; violation from ignorance or negligence without affliction is untainted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: violating with afflicted contempt is tainted; violating out of ignorance or negligence, without affliction, is untainted. Venerable Miào Jìng: with contempt it is tainted; without contempt, untainted.

quiz.q: The English renders this as "a monastic who has attained genuine, verified confidence." How do the lectures explain it?
options: both: a stream-enterer monk with the four kinds of verified faith
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a bodhisattva of pure intention is like a monk who has attained the first fruit and the four kinds of verified faith. Venerable Miào Jìng: a monk with the four verified faiths is really a stream-enterer. The English does not mention the first fruit.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "innate affliction," and what does Venerable Miào Jìng warn?
options: innate affliction is the habitual momentum of greed carried from past lives; Miào Jìng: if after decades as a monastic you are still like this, the excuse no longer holds
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: innate affliction is the habitual momentum of greed brought from past lives — affliction within one's nature. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you've been a monastic for decades and are still like this, you can't say that anymore.

quiz.q: How do the two lectures explain "qí zhǎng" (elders)?
options: Cháng Bǎi: sixty-year-olds and those over seventy; Miào Jìng: sixty may be called "qí," and "zhǎng" means high monastic seniority
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one meaning is people of sixty, the other those over seventy. Venerable Miào Jìng: at sixty one may be called "qí"; "zhǎng" means high monastic seniority.

quiz.q: An exemption is "protecting an unbroken course of wholesome practice." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: being in a meditation or recitation retreat — one may certainly decline
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if one is in the middle of a seven-day meditation or recitation retreat, one may of course decline; for all fourteen of these causes, declining is no violation.

quiz.q: Refusing valuable offerings out of resentment is a tainted violation. What reason does the treatise give?
quiz.why: Refusing out of resentment "constitutes a tainted violation, since it amounts to abandoning the very being making the offering." Venerable Miào Jìng: so a bodhisattva receiving offerings must observe carefully.
